title: What the budget is made of
summary: The main costs for a beginner in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting: coaching, the gun, cartridges, targets, protection, documents and insurance, entry fees and travel.

body.html: Clay shooting, like many sports, has one-off and regular costs. One-off costs are things you buy once in a few years: a gun, glasses, hearing protection, a vest. Regular costs are what you use up at each session: cartridges and targets. Prices differ a lot between countries, regions and grounds, so this lesson gives no amounts, only what a budget is made of.

Coaching. Lessons with a coach are often money well spent at the start. A coach teaches safety, sets up your stance and gun mount, and helps you avoid habits that take long to fix. Many grounds offer a taster session for beginners with the gun, cartridges and targets included.

The gun. A beginner usually starts with a gun hired at the ground and buys their own later. Your own gun is the biggest one-off cost, but it lasts many years. Add a slip (a soft gun cover) or a hard case, a cleaning kit and, where the law requires it, a safe. Renting or buying: Choosing your first gun.

Cartridges and targets are the main regular cost. A round is 25 targets, and each target needs at least one cartridge. Take spares: at a single target you may fire a second shot, so a round can use more cartridges than it has targets. Targets are paid for separately, per target or per round, depending on the ground.

Protection and clothing: safety glasses, earplugs or ear muffs, and later a shooting vest, a cap and comfortable shoes. Glasses and hearing protection are needed from the first session; grounds often lend them.

Documents and insurance. To own a gun, many countries require a firearms permit. For competitions you often also need federation membership or a sports licence. Many countries or clubs require liability insurance (cover for harm you might cause to other people). If you live in the EU and take your own gun to another EU country, you usually need a European Firearms Pass. Without one, you can hire a gun where you are going. Requirements differ from country to country: Travelling with a gun inside the EU.
Competitions and travel. Competitions charge an entry fee. Add travel, accommodation and meals if the event is far away. Club shoots close to home are an affordable way to start competing.

key_points.html: One-off costs: gun, protection, vest, safe.
Regular costs: cartridges and targets; coaching as often as you book it.
A round (25 targets) needs at least as many cartridges; take spares for second shots.
Documents, membership and insurance depend on the country.

did_you_know.html: Under FITASC rules an international competition is 200 targets, shot in rounds of 25, so one such event needs at least as many cartridges, and more with spares.
